correctness.rationale: For common shape \(\alpha\) and slow/fast rates \(a<b\), the exact curvature identity is \((\log f)\prime\prime(x)/(b-a)^2=-(\alpha-1)/t^2+1/[4\cosh^2((t-\log r)/2)]\), where \(t=(b-a)x\) and \(r=wb^\alpha/((1-w)a^\alpha)\). For \(\alpha\le1\) curvature is strictly positive. For \(\alpha>1\), nonpositivity at every positive argument is equivalent to \(\sup_{t>0} t/[2\cosh((t-c)/2)]\le\sqrt{\alpha-1}\), where \(c=\log r\). This function is strictly log-concave, has a unique maximum and tends to zero at both positive-line endpoints; its maximum strictly increases with \(c\), tending to zero and infinity at opposite parameter limits. The unique maximum/tangency equations yield \(t=2\sqrt\alpha\) and \(c=2\sqrt\alpha-2\operatorname{arsinh}(1/\sqrt{\alpha-1})\), the exact threshold. A single positive-curvature interval exists precisely above threshold. The separate degenerate Gamma cases are log-concave exactly for \(\alpha\ge1\). The extracted executable performs 196 finite checks, while the analytic argument, not finite samples, proves the universal statement.

originality.rationale: Primary textual comparisons separate rate alternatives from convolution and from shape mixtures. Yu (2009, Section 2 Example 5) compares Gamma mixtures to reference distributions in relative log-concavity/stochastic order, not the ordinary log-Hessian of a two-rate mixture. Levy (2020, Sections 2-4) computes densities of independent sums, and Mu (2013) characterizes Beta-mixture log-concavity. The identified conference article studies hyper-Erlang convolution; abstract-level material does not give the stated threshold, but its full text was inaccessible and no negative full-text conclusion is asserted. Focused published searches and semantic result searches did not reveal exact, equivalent or stronger coverage; non-detection is not itself proof of novelty.

value.rationale: This is the complete necessary/sufficient classification for equal-shape, two-rate Gamma and fixed-stage two-branch hyper-Erlang mixtures, natural distributional alternatives in reliability modeling. It produces a sharp normalized amplitude threshold depending only on shape rather than absolute rate difference, identifies exactly one positive-log-curvature interval when the condition fails, and shows arbitrary rate closeness can still destroy global log-concavity in remote tails despite convergence in total variation to a log-concave Gamma law. No larger-component generalization or statistical optimality is asserted.
